item.title: From leadership crises to tech outages, can corporations rebuild public trust?
item.description: From cyberattacks to network failures to leadership crises, tech corporations are showing signs of vulnerability. The dramatic resignation and return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has underscored the potential risk of depending on a single leader, both for the company and the entire AI industry. Meanwhile, global outages at Microsoft and a number of US banks have showcased declining public trust in institutions.

item.title: French actor Gérard Depardieu to stand trial on rape charge, lawyer says
item.description: A lawyer representing French actor Gérard Depardieu says he has been ordered to stand trial on a charge of raping a young actress at his Paris home in 2018

item.title: French woman on trial for IS group propaganda tells court she’s ‘ashamed’
item.description: The trial of Émilie König, one of France's most high-profile Islamic State (IS) group recruits, opened in a Paris court on Thursday with the 41-year-old mother of five apologising to her children, mother and the "French nation" for her actions. König travelled in 2012 to Syria, where she appeared in the jihadist group's propaganda videos. She was repatriated to France in 2022.

item.title: Iran live updates: Iranian drone attack killed 2 Italians, Kuwait says
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: Season's eatings! Celebrating Thanksgiving in France
item.description: This Thursday marks Thanksgiving in the United States, the biggest travel holiday of the year there and arguably the most important on US calendars. But here in France, it's just another day. However, Americans living in Paris do try to capture the Thanksgiving spirit, though it can be tricky to track down the turkeys and pies required. Joining us to discuss how Americans do Thanksgiving in Paris is Cordon Bleu-trained chef and the owner of Boneshaker Donuts, Amanda Bankert.

item.title: Madagascar's near-total abortion ban puts women's lives at risk
item.description: November 25 marked the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. Activists argue that tackling gender-based violence also means addressing the wider inequalities that put women at risk, including restrictions on reproductive rights. In Madagascar, abortion is almost entirely banned, even in cases of rape, incest or when a woman's life is at risk. FRANCE 24’s Aurélie Kouman reports on the consequences of the country's strict laws, which force thousands of women to seek unsafe, clandestine procedures.

item.title: Fighting in eastern Congo forces Ebola workers to evacuate, disrupts outbreak response
item.description: Escalating fighting in eastern Congo has forced Ebola response workers to leave affected areas and disrupted efforts to contain the deadliest outbreak in the country, health officials and humanitarian workers said Wednesday. Congo’s Ebola outbreak has infected more than 11,700 people and killed more than 5,700 since it was declared in May, according to the latest government data. FRANCE 24's Emmet Livingstone reports from Kinshasa, DR Congo.

item.title: Moscow drone incursions: Poland to create no-fly zone at Ukraine border
item.description: Poland will soon create a no-fly zone near the Ukrainian border, a deputy defence minister announced on Wednesday, after several incursions into its airspace it blamed on Russia. Poland backs Ukraine as it fights off Russia's near five-year invasion and has repeatedly accused Moscow of seeking to target Kyiv's supporters with drone incursions and other methods.

item.title: Émilie König, 'the muse of the Islamic State group' goes on trial in France
item.description: French anti-terrorism prosecutors once dubbed her "the muse of the Islamic State group". On Thursday, Émilie König appears before a special criminal court in Paris, seeking to convince judges that she has been deradicalised. Originally from western France, König spent a decade in Syria and is accused of being one of the Islamic State group's most active French propagandists. Charged with criminal association with a terrorist organisation, she maintains that she has no blood on her hands.

item.title: New York declares emergency as Thanksgiving storm threatens East Coast
item.description: Gov. Kathy Hochul's office declared a State of Emergency on Thanksgiving.

item.title: Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 12,000 cases as some responders evacuate
item.description: As the fast-moving outbreak continues to spread in eastern Congo, fighting between rebels and the army is disrupting efforts to contain the spread of the disease. (Image credit: Sebastien Kitsa Musayi)

item.title: French actor Gérard Depardieu to face trial for alleged rape of actress Charlotte Arnould
item.description: French actor Gérard ​Depardieu will face trial on charges of raping actress Charlotte Arnould in 2018, his lawyer said on ​Thursday. Depardieu, one of the leading faces of French ​cinema, has denied wrongdoing in the case.

item.title: Scotland's top medical chief resigns on health grounds
item.description: Scotland's chief medical officer has resigned, stating he does not "currently enjoy the good mental health necessary to continue" in the position.

item.title: Housing crisis on the ballot: Anger boils over ahead of Spanish election
item.description: Spaniards head to the polls on Sunday in a general election that was called after street protests for affordable housing. Anger bubbled over after 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal was evicted from her home of seven decades and two decrees to tackle the housing crisis were rejected by parliament. In calling the snap election, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is hoping the housing issue can galvanise his left-wing base.

item.title: 'Europe has two kinds of countries: Small countries & those that haven’t yet realised they’re small’
item.description: “The implications of having the far right in power in Brussels are enormous,” warns Sophie Pornschlegel, Senior Advisor at the European Policy Centre. With elections approaching in several EU member states, including France and Italy, what would a growing number of far-right, Eurosceptic governments mean for the EU budget, relations between European institutions, common legislation and support for Ukraine? Could Giorgia Meloni could adopt a more radical stance? “The whole idea of the EU is to have a common legislation that is then applied in 27 member states. Otherwise, what is the point of having the EU?”

item.title: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
item.description: Leader Kim Jong Un reportedly visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons to cope with threats from the U.S. and South Korea. (Image credit: Korean Central News Agency)

item.title: 'As humans we feel spiritually homeless': Turkish author Ece Temelkuran on belonging
item.description: For Ece Temelkuran, the human condition is "unhomed". Speaking to FRANCE 24, the Turkish author cites the rise of artificial intelligence, climate change and the authoritarian drift as reasons why one may no longer recognise the place one calls home. This feeling of "spiritual homelessness" is something she explores in her latest book, "Nation of Strangers: Rebuilding Home in the 21st Century". Most of all, she highlights the importance of human connection: "In survival mode (...) you live on the kindness of others."

item.title: Channel 4 says its documentary allowing Huw Edwards to speak was 'an important film to make'
item.description: Channel 4 has said its new documentary giving disgraced former newsreader Huw Edwards the chance to speak about his crimes was "an important film to make".

item.title: Security incident reported at Royal Navy headquarters
item.description: Police responded to what appears to have been a hoax bomb threat at a Royal Navy training site.

item.title: Israel threatens to displace one million Palestinians in Gaza unless Hamas disarms
item.description: Israel's defence minister on Thursday threatened to forcibly displace one million Palestinians in Gaza if Hamas does not move to voluntarily surrender its weapons, as previously promised.

item.title: Charity set up in honour of Princess Diana placed into administration
item.description: A charity set up in tribute to the late Princess Diana has been placed into administration.

item.title: EU chief urges leaders to 'compromise' for budget deal by year-end
item.description: European Council President Antonio Costa urged European leaders to seek compromise on the bloc's long-term budget at a summit Thursday, as Brussels pushes to lock in the plans before next year's French election where far-right leader Marine Le Pen is leading in opinion polls. "Now it is time for all of the leaders to participate in this debate with an open mind, a constructive approach, and a sense of compromise. Because we need to approve this budget timely. That means by the end of this year," Costa said. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels, Belgium.

item.title: French far-right leader Bardella faces fresh anti-Semitism accusations in media reports
item.description: French far-right leader ⁠Jordan Bardella faced fresh ​accusations of past antisemitic remarks on Thursday, as French media published an additional ​trove of comments purportedly made in chats from when he was a teenager in 2013. The initial allegations against Bardella, the president of the far-right National Rally party, were published ​by investigative outlet ‌Mediapart in September. It reported that he had made ⁠a slew of antisemitic and conspiratorial comments. Bardella denies making antisemitic remarks. FRANCE 24's French Politics Editor Marc Perelman tells us more.

item.title: Egypt: 31 people killed in Cairo after fuel truck overturns
item.description: A fire broke out on a busy highway in Egypt’s capital, Cairo, on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people after a fuel truck reportedly overturned. The suspected driver was arrested on Thursday, according to Egypt’s public prosecutor’s office.

item.title: Alleged Islamic State group propagandist Emily Konig on trial in France
item.description: Accused of being one of the Islamic State group's most active French propagandists, Emily Konig went on trial in Paris on Thursday. Originally from Brittany, Konig spent a decade in Syria before returning to France in 2022. She is charged with criminal association with a terrorist organisation and faces up to 30 years in prison if convicted. FRANCE 24's Luke Shrago is following the trial in Paris and joins us to explain the defence's strategy.

item.title: French media publish fresh claims of far-right leader Bardella's 'anti-Semitic torrent'
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Thursday, November 26: French media outlets Mediapart and Le Monde publish an additional trove of messages purporting to show far-right leader Jordan Bardella's rampant anti-Semitic thoughts as a young member of the party in 2013. Also: France holds the first trial of a female jihadist, Émilie König. Kilmar Abrego Garcia, once the face of Donald Trump's brutal mass deportations, arrives in Spain. Plus: we find out why the rich world is in the midst of a "sex recession."

item.title: France: Senior officials investigated over suspected leaks to far-right National Rally
item.description: Two senior figures in France have been caught up in an investigation into suspected leaks to the far-right National Rally. The prefect of the Loiret and former top official at the Interior Ministry, Hugues Moutouh, has been removed from his post after being suspected of passing on confidential information about investigations. A deputy prosecutor in Paris, who was found at the party's headquarters during a police search, is now also under administrative inquiry

item.title: EU Budget talks: France seeks to protect Common Agricultural Policy subsidies
item.description: Leaders from EU countries are meeting in Brussels on Thursday and Friday for another round of talks on the EU's next multi-year budget. For France, the main aim of the negotiations is to prevent a reduction in the funding allocated to the Common Agricultural Policy, a subsidy vital for French agriculture – a position Macron made clear in a meeting with farmers unions in Paris on Wednesday.

item.title: Trump unveils new tariffs on 14 trade partners over 'unfair' industrial capacity
item.description: US President Donald Trump fired a new tariff salvo on Wednesday on 14 major trading partners including China, Japan and the European Union, undeterred in his protectionist push by the losses his Republican Party suffered in US midterm elections. His administration proposed new maximum potential rates of 20% to 40% to counter excess industrial capacity that it says these countries are promoting.

item.title: 'King tide' waves batter California coast, soaking San Francisco
item.description: Massive waves carried on king tides battered California's coast Wednesday, prompting evacuations and soaking San Francisco, but sparing feared mass disruptions to Thanksgiving holiday travel. San Francisco already recorded its highest November water levels in more than 40 years on Tuesday morning, according to the National Weather Service.

item.title: 'Sacré sel': France's love of salt
item.description: We take a look at a salt scandal that is rocking the UK, after Maldon sea salt was found to come, in part, from rock salt imported from Germany. We also discuss France's relationship to salt (le sel) and the different kinds in France, from fleur de sel to sel gris. Finally, we look at French history and expressions about salt.
